title: Load-adaptive control for quadruped mobile manipulation platforms
topics: Control and Dynamics of Mobile Robots
abstract: Abstract Currently, quadruped robots are widely used in diverse scenarios due to their high mobility, creating a demand for more advanced interaction capabilities. This study proposes a whole-body planning and control framework that integrates adaptive control into a hierarchical model predictive control (MPC) and whole-body control (WBC) structure, enhancing the environmental adaptability and interaction performance of quadruped mobile manipulators. Key innovations include: a recursive least squares and feedforward compensation strategy for accurate end-effector force estimation; relaxed barrier functions embedded in the MPC to combine dynamic obstacle avoidance with adaptive control; and a WBC-based priority hierarchy to enforce critical constraints. Validated in Gazebo simulation and on the B1-Z1 platform, the method allows the robot to handle unknown loads up to 3 kg and maintain tracking errors under 2 cm despite 35 N external disturbances. It also demonstrates strong adaptability in non-uniform object transportation, providing a reliable solution for unstructured environments.

title: Adaptive Control to Derive a Ride Comfort Mode in Rotorcraft
venue: Journal of the American Helicopter Society
abstract: Prolonged turbulence can result in the experience of kinetosis (motion sickness) among helicopter passengers, thereby negatively impacting the ride comfort of the flight. To address this issue, a comfort mode, analogous to that employed in the automotive industry, can be implemented for the helicopter flight control system. In order to design the comfort mode, a closed-loop reference model of the helicopter is derived that leads to minimal kinetosis at given turbulence intensities. Adaptive control laws from the model reference adaptive control framework are employed and evaluated to modify nominal closed-loop behavior in accordance with the derived reference model when the comfort mode is engaged. The efficacy of adaptive control laws in reducing the severity of kinetosis is demonstrated through simulations. These control laws compensate for the negative effects of turbulence, thereby contributing to a more comfortable flight experience.

title: Methods of adaptive control of iterative decoding of turbo codes
abstract: The rapid development of 5G and 6G wireless networks has put forward strict requirements for the delay of channel decoding, which has actualised the task of reducing the computational complexity of iterative turbo decoders without losing noise immunity. The purpose of the study was to systematise, classify, and compare methods of adaptive control of the number of iterations of the turbo decoder, in particular, the classical criteria for early stop and the neural network adaptive approach. Methods of comparative theoretical analysis, analytical classification of criteria by convergence indicator type, and assessment of computational complexity based on published results for codes compatible with the 4G standard were applied. Classification of criteria by the type of convergence indicator and by the type of implementation was proposed. It was found that classical criteria based on hard solutions, ratio and sign difference, cross-entropy, and average reliability of soft solutions reduced the average number of iterations by 30-55% with a slight degradation in the bit error rate. It was found that improvements in the efficiency of the criteria were accompanied by increased demands on memory and computing resources. It was shown that the neural network adaptive method integrated into the model-oriented decoder reduced the average number of iterations by 60-75% due to the fact that the stop threshold was trained together with the decoder weights and automatically adapted to channel ...

title: ON ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF ELECTRIC VEHICLES CONSIDERING OPERATING CONDITIONS
venue: International Multidisciplinary Journal for Research & Development
abstract: Electric cars drive in a lot of different conditions, which change how they work and how much energy they use all the time. The slope of the road, the weight of the vehicle, the state of charge of the battery, and the driver's demand all add uncertainty that makes traditional fixed-parameter control strategies less effective. These kinds of controllers might work well in normal situations, but they often don't work as well in real life. This makes batteries work harder and uses more energy. This paper presents an adaptive control framework for electric vehicles that explicitly addresses varying operational conditions. A control-oriented model of the electric vehicle is developed, incorporating the essential interactions between longitudinal vehicle dynamics, the electric drivetrain, and the battery energy system. This formulation posits that the control problem is characterized by parameters that are often uncertain and subject to temporal variation, in addition to practical constraints on motor torque and battery operational limits. The proposed method incorporates knowledge of operating conditions directly into the control strategy, enabling real-time adjustments of control parameters in response to variations in road conditions, vehicle mass, and battery status. The function of the controller is track vehicle speed and make it more energy-efficient while also limiting how much power the battery needs. It does this by changing how much torque the traction motor has. The for...

title: A deep reinforcement learning framework for adaptive control charts
abstract: This study introduces a reinforcement-learning-based sequential sampling framework for adaptive control charts. Traditional adaptive charts improve monitoring efficiency by adjusting sampling effort according to the current chart state, but they require manually specified decision regions and region-to-action assignments. This becomes difficult when many sample-size and sampling-interval combinations are available. The proposed method preserves the classical EWMA statistic and control-limit signaling rule, while using a deep Q-network (DQN) to learn the adaptive sampling policy for a variable sample size and sampling interval (VSSI) control chart. At each sampling epoch, the agent (DQN) observes the monitoring state and selects the sampling pair. The general design considers a 70-action space formed from ten candidate sample sizes and seven candidate sampling intervals, with the reward function balancing false-alarm control, detection speed, and sampling-resource constraints. Numerical results show that the DQN-VSSI-EWMA chart satisfies the target average sample size and average sampling interval. The learned policy also exhibits clear VSSI-type behavior, using lower sampling effort in low-risk states and increasing monitoring intensity as the EWMA statistic approaches the control limit. A restricted four-action DQN is also compared with a traditional four-level VSSI-EWMA chart using the same sampling actions. This comparison shows that the DQN can learn a feasible adaptive s...

title: Self-Correcting Quantum Circuits via Adaptive Control
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of self-correcting quantum circuits, a paradigm shift from traditional passive error correction strategies in quantum computing. The core concept involves creating quantum circuits capable of autonomously detecting and rectifying errors through adaptive control mechanisms. This is achieved by utilizing ancillary qubits for real-time monitoring of circuit dynamics and employing a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to dynamically adjust control pulses, thereby minimizing decoherence and maximizing quantum fidelity. The proposed approach moves beyond passive correction, introducing an active system that responds intelligently to errors as they occur. The theoretical framework and the underlying mechanisms are detailed, laying the groundwork for future research and development in robust and resilient quantum computation. The key advancements lie in the integration of dynamic monitoring and adaptive control, offering a potentially significant step towards fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Current Tracking Adaptive Control of Brushless DC Motors
venue: International Journal of Adaptive Control and Signal Processing
abstract: ABSTRACT In this article, the practical problem of current tracking for Brushless Direct Current motors is approached. The main feature of the contribution lies in the fact that uncertainty in the parameters of the motor's model is considered. This lack of knowledge is compensated by proposing an adaptive control scheme that directly deals with the uncertainty in the electrical parameters without requiring any knowledge, neither of the mechanical parameters nor the load torque, as long as this external disturbance remains bounded. The strength of the proposed control scheme appears from the passivity‐based decomposition of the motor's model allowing robust control of the electrical subsystem without requiring mechanical information, providing the rotor speed remains bounded. Moreover, achievement of the control objective does not rely on estimated parameter convergence to the real values. The stability properties of the proposed scheme are mathematically proved using classical results from the passivity and the adaptive control theories, which makes it attractive from a practical perspective. Moreover, it exhibits a simple structure and is easy to tune. The usefulness of the contribution is validated in an experimental setting using the BLY344S‐240V‐3000 motor manufactured by Anaheim Automation.

title: Adaptive Control of Heterogeneous Platoons With Guaranteed Collision Avoidance
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

inst.name: Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi
Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi

abstract: This work proposes a guaranteed collision avoidance framework for Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control of a vehicular platoon characterized by unidirectional communication and heterogeneous parameters. In the proposed framework, the actual (heterogeneous) platoon is made to converge to a reference (homogeneous) platoon via adaptive laws designed using of set-theoretic model reference adaptive control. Yet, in contrast to the state-of-art that is based on ensuring collision avoidance on the reference platoon dynamics only, the approach we propose can ensure collision avoidance on the actual platoon dynamics. This result is possible thanks to the introduction of a novel concept of virtual platoon, only used for analysis, but that does not interact with the actual platoon. The stability and convergence properties of the proposed framework are established using Lyapunov-based analysis in conjunction with the aforementioned virtual platoon concept. Simulation results further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Non-linear Dynamics Systems Adaptive Control Algorithm
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive control algorithm designed for non-linear dynamics systems. Traditional control methods often struggle with complex, non-linear systems, requiring extensive tuning and potentially leading to instability. This research introduces a dynamic topology control strategy that leverages the inherent structure of the system to dynamically adjust control parameters, thereby enhancing system stability and responsiveness. The core mechanism centers on the concept of "dynamic topology" – a novel approach to control parameter mapping that adapts to environmental changes. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in system performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving rapid parameter changes and fluctuating environmental conditions. This work represents a significant advancement in adaptive control techniques, offering a robust and adaptable solution for a wide range of non-linear systems.

title: Adaptive control system for multichannel nonlinear dynamical plants
venue: Dynamics of Complex Systems - XXI century
abstract: A class of nonlinear plants characterized by multiple control channels is considered, where the same output objective can be achieved through different combinations of control inputs. As a representative example, a doubly-fed inductor motor is analyzed, for which six control variables are available: two voltage amplitudes, two frequencies, and two controllable phase shifts. These inputs enable regulation of the motor’s angular velocity, r otation angle, and electromagnetic torque. For the synthesis of control laws, linear -system theory is employed with parameters fixed at values defined by the steady -state operating point of the nonlinear plant. The proposed approach utilizes the redundancy of control inputs, since variations in speed or position can be achieved with different combinations of control variables. Although operating conditions change during regulation, which would normally require adaptation of cont rol-law parameters, in the proposed method these parameters remain constant. Instead, appropriate coordinated adjustments of supply frequency and voltage amplitude are selected to achieve the desired speed (proportional to the frequency difference) while keeping controller parameters unchanged.

title: Spinelli & Lupker - No evidence for context-specific adaptive control
Non-Linear Dynamical Systems Adaptive Control Theory
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive control theory for non-linear dynamical systems, utilizing a dynamic adjustment of control parameters to achieve optimal system performance. Traditional control methods often rely on static parameter settings, offering limited adaptability to system dynamics. We introduce a system-based approach, employing an adaptive algorithm, to dynamically adjust control parameters, thereby enhancing system responsiveness and robustness. The core mechanism centers on the iterative refinement of control parameters based on real-time system feedback, enabling the system to converge to optimal operating points. This research focuses on addressing the inherent challenges of non-linear systems and provides a framework for achieving superior control performance in dynamic environments.

title: Adaptive Control Systems Utilizing Quantum Feedback Loops
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of adaptive control systems utilizing quantum feedback loops for achieving enhanced control performance in complex dynamic systems. Classical control methods often struggle with the inherent uncertainties and nonlinearities present in many real-world systems. We propose a novel approach that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum measurement and feedback, to directly influence system dynamics. The core concept involves creating a quantum feedback loop where continuous measurements of the system's state are processed through a quantum measurement apparatus and used to modify the control input. The utilization of quantum entanglement is explored as a mechanism to improve the sensitivity of the feedback loop, potentially leading to dramatically faster and more precise control compared to traditional approaches. This research introduces a theoretical framework and explores the mathematical foundations for such systems, highlighting key advantages and potential challenges. The presented model demonstrates the feasibility of adapting control strategies in real-time, based on quantum measurements, for improved system regulation and stability. This work represents a significant step towards exploring the application of quantum technologies in control engineering.

title: Safe and Scalable Minimax Adaptive Control of Positive Systems
topics: Stability and Control of Uncertain Systems
abstract: This paper studies minimax adaptive control of positive linear systems with fixed unknown dynamics and nonnegative disturbances. We reformulate the problem by compressing the historical data into a vector and a positivity-induced consistency set containing the models compatible with the observations. Together with the physical state, these quantities form a sufficient information state and yield an exact reformulation as a standard minimax dynamic game. We allow the admissible input set to adapt to the current consistency set, ensuring positivity for every remaining feasible model. As inconsistent models are eliminated, the input set can expand, allowing less cautious control actions. For finite model sets, we derive an explicit solution to the Bellman inequality and construct a safe and stabilizing certainty-equivalence controller with robustness guarantees. The framework also accommodates structured classes of continuum model uncertainty whose consistency sets admit fixed, finite-dimensional representations, enabling scalable information-state updates.

title: MODEL REFERENCE ADAPTIVE CONTROL STRATEGY FOR PROCESS PLANT.
venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
abstract: Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) is an advanced adaptive control technique developed to ensure desired system performance in the presence of uncertainties, disturbances, and time-varying parameters.This paper presents a comprehensive review of MRAC, focusing on its fundamental principles, structures, adaptation mechanisms, and practical applications.In MRAC, the control objective is achieved by forcing the plant output to track a predefined reference model through continuous adjustment of controller parameters based on tracking error.The study discusses the two primary MRAC schemes-direct and indirect-along with commonly used adaptation laws such as the MIT rule and Lyapunov-based methods, which ensure system stability.Various MRAC architectures, including robust and modified versions, are also explored to address challenges like noise sensitivity and unmodeled dynamics.Furthermore, the paper highlights the wide range of applications of MRAC in fields such as aerospace, robotics, automotive systems, process control, and power electronics.Recent advancements involving the integration of artificial intelligence techniques, such as neural networks and reinforcement learning, are also reviewed.The paper concludes by addressing existing limitations and emphasizing future research directions toward intelligent and robust adaptive control systems.

title: Based on Adaptive Control Chaotic System Modeling and Control
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling and controlling chaotic systems using adaptive control techniques. The core of the method lies in dynamically adjusting control parameters based on the observed state of the chaotic system. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameters, which are unsuitable for the inherently unpredictable nature of chaotic systems. This approach addresses this limitation by leveraging feedback from the system itself to continuously refine the control strategy. The proposed strategy aims to achieve stable control by adapting to the evolving dynamics of the chaotic system. The theoretical framework is outlined, and the control algorithm is described in detail. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive control method in stabilizing a representative chaotic system. The key contribution is a robust and adaptable control scheme, offering a promising solution for controlling complex, nonlinear systems.

title: Learning Adaptive Control for Safe Collaborative Autonomous Driving
venue: ScholarWorks @ UTRGV (The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley)

inst.name: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

abstract: Connected autonomous vehicles improve urban driving through collaborative perception via Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication. Frameworks such as V2Xverse leverage this collaboration for planning and perception, yet their controllers rely on fixed parameters that cannot adapt to varying traffic. Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) enforce safety by constraining actions within a safe set, but a fixed barrier gain imposes a single operating point: conservative settings reduce throughput while permissive settings under-react to hazards. This research proposes an adaptive CBF framework that learns state-dependent, class-specific barrier gains via constrained Reinforcement Learning (RL). A compact policy outputs separate gains for vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles, parameterizing a CBF quadratic program that modifies only longitudinal control. Training uses constrained PPO with a PID-based Lagrangian multiplier to satisfy a safety cost budget. We evaluated 315 closed-loop trials across 105 routes in CARLA Town05, comparing the adaptive policy against an unfiltered proportional-integral-derivative (PID) baseline and a fixed-gain CBF filter under identical perception and planning. The adaptive method achieves the highest driving score of 75.81, and reduces collisions per route by 80.3% relative to the unfiltered baseline and by 25.9% relative to the fixed CBF filter, and increases the collision-free route rate to 59.7% while maintaining the best route completion at 90.8%. title: Adaptive Control Volume Model for Predicting Pseudoshock Properties
abstract: An adaptive control volume (ACV) is developed to model pseudoshock properties as a function of the backpressure for supersonic internal flows. The formulation accounts for outlet Mach number nonuniformity using two primary independent variables and can be formulated under either attached or separated flow assumptions. The model is applied to a Mach 2 pseudoshock in a rectangular duct with area change and is validated against computational fluid dynamics solutions. Results demonstrate accurate prediction of the area-averaged Mach number and mass-averaged total pressure over a wide range of backpressures. Sensitivity analyses show that the solution is weakly dependent on the nonuniformity parameter once sufficiently large, while the turbulent momentum transport parameter strongly influences total pressure losses. Beyond validation, the ACV model provides insight into pseudoshock physics, permits reliable prediction of outlet quantities using only wall static pressure measurements, and offers potential for low-cost system monitoring and control in high-speed vehicle applications.

title: Geometric Chaos through Adaptive Control of Parameter Space
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper investigates the phenomenon of geometric chaos – a state of dynamical systems characterized by unpredictable and seemingly random fluctuations – through the development of an adaptive control system. Traditional approaches to chaos theory often rely on fixed parameter spaces, limiting the system's ability to exhibit dynamic and evolving behavior. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging adaptive control to maintain geometric chaos, offering a pathway to systems that continuously generate novel and unpredictable patterns. The core mechanism centers on a control algorithm that dynamically adjusts parameters, thereby influencing the system's trajectory and preserving the inherent chaotic dynamics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulation and analysis, showcasing its ability to generate complex and persistent geometric chaos.

title: Formal Verification of Adaptive Control Systems with Symbolic Execution
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Adaptive control systems are widely used in applications where the system dynamics are uncertain or time-varying. However, verifying the correctness and safety of these systems is a significant challenge due to the inherent adaptation process. This paper presents a novel approach to formally verify adaptive control systems by integrating symbolic execution with formal verification. The core idea is to systematically explore the system's behavior under different operating conditions using symbolic execution, generating a symbolic representation of the adaptive control policy. Subsequently, model checking is employed to rigorously verify the safety and performance properties of this policy. This method provides a rigorous and comprehensive means of guaranteeing the desired behavior of adaptive control systems, addressing a critical gap in the field. The key contributions lie in the seamless integration of symbolic execution's exploration capabilities with model checking's verification rigor, leading to a practical and effective approach for adaptive control formal verification.

title: Adaptive Control Strategy Based on Time Series Prediction
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel adaptive control strategy leveraging time series prediction models to enhance system performance. The core idea is to predict the future state of a control system using a time series model, and subsequently, adapt the control strategy based on these predictions. Traditional adaptive control methods often rely on heuristic rules or trial-and-error, which can be inefficient and suboptimal. This approach introduces a predictive element, allowing the controller to anticipate changes in the system and proactively adjust its parameters. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through a theoretical framework and analysis, highlighting its potential benefits over conventional adaptive control techniques. This work provides a foundation for developing more robust and efficient control systems across various applications where dynamic system behavior is prevalent.

title: APPLICATION OF SENSORS IN THE ADAPTIVE CONTROL OF A MECHATRONIC MODULE ACTUATOR
abstract: Modern gripper systems used in mechatronic modules still face significant challenges when handling objects of unknown mass in unstructured working environments. Conventional rigid grippers typically operate through simple opening and closing mechanisms and lack adaptive tactile feedback. Consequently, object slippage, excessive gripping force, and instability during manipulation may occur. Therefore, there is a growing demand for intelligent, adaptive, and cost-effective gripping elements. This paper addresses the development of a relatively low-cost adaptive robotic gripper capable of detecting object slippage in real time and intelligently adjusting the gripping force through sensor integration and machine-learning-based control algorithms. This study proposes a practical solution to the challenges associated with handling and transferring objects in manufacturing, warehousing, and logistics by integrating FSR force sensors with an embedded AI model deployed on a microcontroller.

title: Multi-Scale Dynamics Optimization via Adaptive Control
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive control strategies within multi-scale dynamics simulations to enhance energy utilization and system adaptability. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed control parameters, limiting the simulation's ability to accurately model complex environments. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts control parameters based on real-time system feedback, resulting in more efficient energy management and improved system response. This work demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through the simulation of a simplified, yet representative, biological system. The core claim centers on the utilization of adaptive control to achieve superior performance compared to static control methods.

title: THE MODEL LEARNING ALGORITHM AS APPLIED TO ADAPTIVE CONTROL SYSTEM
venue: Bulletin of the Saint Petersburg State Institute of Technology (Technical University)
abstract: An algorithm of model learning (parameters tuning) for adaptive control systems is considered. The algorithm provides determination, using steepest descent method, of the parameters (coefficients) of model equation that follow-up the variable in time plant parameters (coefficients). The scanning procedure to minimize the objective function is based on «Golden ratio» method. The practical examples are provided to demonstrate the algorithm’s efficiency. The stability of parameters adjusting (model learning) process is shown.

title: Design of Combined Adaptive Control Systems for Power Converters
abstract: Abstract This paper presents an approach to designing combined adaptive control systems for power converters that integrate a classical PID controller with a reinforcement-learning agent. The agent, based on an artificial neural network, generates an optimal control action in real time, while a robustness module ensures safe switching to known-stable settings of the classical controller when parameters exceed allowable limits. The architecture of the feedforward artificial neural network and the methodology for organizing reinforcement learning using a Thompson sampling strategy in a computer simulation environment are described. The proposed approach is validated on a double-conversion uninterruptible power supply: simulation results obtained in MATLAB/Simulink and experimental studies using a Processor-in-the-Loop methodology with deployment of the control system on an STM32 F7-series (ARM Cortex-M7) microcontroller are presented. The universality of the proposed approach and its applicability to other classes of power converters are discussed, including semiconductor switching devices for voltage regulation in transmission lines and at 6–10/0.4 kV substations.

title: Adaptive control of a robotic exoskeleton for enhanced knee rehabilitation
abstract: Variable stiffness actuators (VSAs) offer significant potential for diverse applications due to their ability to adjust stiffness in response to operational requirements. The proposed VSA comprises 12 pairs of outer pulleys and six pairs of inner pulleys, uniformly arranged around a central axis and connected in series to a spring via a cable. Rotation of the inner pulleys around the center extends the spring, generating an elastic force that is transmitted through the cable to the output link, producing output torque and stiffness. The output stiffness varies with the angle of rotation, posing challenges for control system design. This study proposes machine learning-based approaches to achieve accurate and low-latency control. Specifically, neural network models are developed to estimate the spring preload at various actuator positions, enabling precise control of the desired stiffness. The results show that the Feedforward Neural Network enables the actuator to achieve a stiffness with a root-mean-square error of 0.0073 Ncm/degree.

title: A composite robust adaptive control of uncertain nonlinear systems
topics: Stability and Control of Uncertain Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel composite robust adaptive control (CRAC) framework for nonlinear systems subject to parameter uncertainties and plant perturbations. Unlike conventional adaptive control schemes, which typically address only parameter uncertainties and require the stringent persistent excitation (PE) condition for parameter convergence, the proposed method seamlessly integrates a direct adaptation mechanism based on tracking errors with an indirect adaptation mechanism based on identification errors. Under unknown bounded disturbances, the proposed CRAC scheme ensures the uniform ultimate boundedness of all closed-loop signals. Remarkably, this basic robustness is achieved by exploiting the informative transient responses induced by non-zero initial conditions, thereby relaxing the need for persistent motion or external dither signals. Furthermore, when the filtered regressor satisfies the PE condition and the filtering gain is constant, the filtering dynamics are input-to-state stable with respect to external disturbances, and the filtered disturbance converges to zero if the original disturbance vanishes. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is validated through numerical simulations on a servo motor system.

title: Robust Fixed-Time Model Reference Adaptive Control

inst.name: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

topics: Stability and Control of Uncertain Systems
abstract: This article proposes a Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) strategy to achieve fixed-time convergence of parameter estimation and tracking errors for unknown linear time-invariant systems, without relying on the persistence of excitation condition. Instead, it employs a less restrictive initial/interval excitation condition on the regressor matrix, enhancing practicality and ease of implementation in real-world scenarios. Our primary contribution is a novel parameter update law within the indirect MRAC framework, ensuring that parameter estimates converge within a fixed time, once the initial/interval excitation condition is met. This approach simplifies the practical requirements for adaptive control while guaranteeing robust performance against parameter uncertainty and external disturbances. Simulation results provide a comparison with the current literature to validate the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Adaptive Control and Synchronization of a Generalized Lotka-Volterra System
topics: Mathematical and Theoretical Epidemiology and Ecology Models
abstract: The Lotka-Volterra equations are a system of equations proposed to provide a simplified model of twospecies predator-prey population dynamics. In this paper, we investigate the problem of adaptive chaoscontrol and synchronization of a generalized Lotka-Volterra system discovered by Samardzija and Greller(1988). The Samardzija-Greller model is a two-predator, one-prey generalization of the Lotka-Volterrasystem. First, adaptive control laws are designed to stabilize the generalized Lotka-Volterra system to itsunstable equilibrium point at the origin based on the adaptive control theory and Lyapunov stabilitytheory. Then adaptive control laws are derived to achieve global chaos synchronization of identicalgeneralized Lotka-Volterra systems with unknown parameters. Numerical simulations are shown tovalidate and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed adaptive control and synchronization schemesfor the generalized Lotka-Volterra system.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology-Driven Adaptive Control Algorithm
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive control algorithm based on dynamic topology structures, designed to optimize and control complex systems efficiently. Traditional control methods rely on manually designed models, which are often inefficient. This algorithm leverages dynamic topology to automatically adjust the system's topology, enabling rapid optimization and system modeling. The core mechanism involves systematically manipulating the topology to achieve desired control performance. This approach offers a significant advancement in control system design, particularly for systems exhibiting dynamic behavior. The paper details the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation, and potential applications.

title: Magnetic Reconnections Stochastic-Adaptive Control for Plasma Fusion
abstract: Abstract In the paper presented a comprehensive investigation into a novel heating mechanism for pulsed fusion devices, specifically the Pulsed Reconnection Engine (PRE) applied to a Spheromak configuration. Conventional Ohmic heating becomes inefficient at reactor temperatures because classical plasma parallel resistivity drops according to the Spitzer relationship ( η S ∝ T e −3/2 ). Consequently, Compact Toroids often stall before reaching ignition temperatures, as they cannot overcome the radiation barrier, where impurity losses exceed heating power. To overcome this fundamental limit without resorting to expensive and bulky auxiliary heating methods like Neutral Beam Injection (NBI), we propose an Adaptive Stochastic Resonance (SR) control strategy. This system actively modulates an effective anomalous resistivity – physically realizable via Radio Frequency (RF) wave injection or Lower Hybrid Current Drive (LHCD) – to trigger magnetic reconnection events synchronized with the plasma’s natural magnetohydrodynamic modes. Using a rigorous 0D/2D two-fluid energy-balance model with realistic confinement assumptions ( τ E = 0.1 s ), we demonstrate four key results: (1) The validity of a resistive diffusion model for tracking thermal evolution in force-free magnetic configurations; (2) The thermodynamic necessity of a two-fluid approach to capture Ion-Electron Decoupling; (3) The capability of SR control to trigger simultaneous multi-site reconnections, enabling Ohmic-like igni...

title: High-Dimensional Topological Mapping for Dynamic Adaptive Control
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high-dimensional topological mapping technique designed for dynamic adaptive control of complex systems. Traditional topological mapping methods often struggle with high-dimensional data due to computational complexity and limited applicability. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the topological structure of the system based on the current state, enabling efficient optimization and control. The core mechanism involves applying a dynamic mapping algorithm to the high-dimensional representation of the system, iteratively refining the topology to achieve optimal performance. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations involving a simulated neural network, showcasing significant improvements in control precision and system stability compared to existing techniques. The key contribution lies in the method's ability to automatically adapt the topology to evolving system dynamics, offering a promising pathway toward more robust and adaptable control systems.

title: Dynamic Topology and Reinforcement Learning: Adaptive Control Strategies
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic application of dynamic topology and reinforcement learning to construct adaptive control strategies for dynamic systems. Traditional reinforcement learning often relies on pre-defined policies, limiting the system's adaptability. Dynamic topology, conversely, offers a mechanism for self-adapting control strategies, mitigating the limitations of static policies. This research investigates a novel framework incorporating both techniques, aiming to optimize system stability through dynamically adjusted control. We present a theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential of this approach. The core claim is that leveraging dynamic topology enables a more robust and adaptable control system compared to traditional methods.

title: Non-Linear Chaos Systems Adaptive Control Theory
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear chaos theory and adaptive control techniques to achieve robust and responsive control over complex systems. The core of our approach centers on utilizing dynamic probability fields and adaptive learning algorithms to stabilize and modulate the behavior of chaotic systems. We introduce a novel framework predicated on the inherent unpredictability of non-linear dynamics, offering a new methodology for manipulating these systems. The theoretical foundation leverages established concepts from chaos theory, dynamic systems theory, and adaptive control, demonstrating the potential for significant advancements in system stability and control. This work presents a practical implementation of this theory, demonstrating its effectiveness through a focused examination of a specific, albeit simplified, example. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: On the ℒ1 Norm Minimization in Adaptive Control of Launch Vehicles
venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
topics: Stability and Control of Uncertain Systems
abstract: The present paper analyses an ℒ1 adaptive control procedure for the control of launch vehicles. A crucial step in the ℒ1 adaptive control design methodology is the minimization of the ℒ1-norm of a specific system, which depends on the launcher model and a stable filter. The lower this norm is, the better it guarantees robustness properties with respect to modeling uncertainties and parameter variations of the launcher dynamics. The paper focuses on determining a numerically reliable methodology for minimizing this norm. It is proven that the parameters of the optimal ℒ1 adaptive controller may be obtained by solving a specific system of matrix inequalities. The proposed procedure is illustrated and validated by a case study for the VEGA launch vehicle.

title: Title: Adaptive Control of Quantum Error Correction Codes
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical challenge in quantum computing, demanding sophisticated control systems. This paper investigates a novel adaptive control system for quantum error correction codes, dynamically adjusting code complexity based on observed error rates. We propose a feedback loop that optimizes the code's parameters to minimize the impact of errors. This research addresses the limitations of traditional fixed-parameter approaches, offering a real-time optimization strategy for improved error mitigation. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of code complexity to proactively combat errors, ultimately enhancing the fidelity of quantum computations.

title: Requisites for applying adaptive control of safety lead time
abstract: Purpose A fundamental manufacturing challenge is how to dimension safety buffers effectively, particularly in today’s challenging competitive environment with increased focus on delivery capability and cost-efficiency. An adaptive approach is suggested to overcome such challenges, but no approach is effective unless applied. The purpose of this study is to explore the requisites for applying adaptive control of safety lead time in manufacturing companies. Design/methodology/approach An interactive, case-based research approach identified requisites – practical aspects to consider – for developing and applying adaptive control of safety lead time among four manufacturing companies. Findings A framework was developed comprising nine propositions on interlinked requisites for understanding cause-and-effect relationships, metrics and measuring, balancing performance variables and organizing for control. The framework is the first step of theory-building. Research limitations/implications The framework complements the literature beyond the conceptual idea of an adaptive control approach, positioned within the production planning process. Extending performance management literature to safety buffer control contributes to understanding and terminology. A metric, balancing delivery capability risk and cost risk to support application, is proposed. title: Chaos synchronization of the Tuberculosis model via adaptive control

inst.name: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University

topics: Mathematical and Theoretical Epidemiology and Ecology Models
abstract: In this paper, we establish chaos synchronization of the chaotic model of Tuberculosis(TB) via adaptive control technique. The Tuberculosis model uses susceptible, exposed, infected and recovered compartments and captures the latent stage of TB which helps in providing a more realistic description and condition of the transmission of TB. The non-linear dynamical characteristics are explained in detail using bifurcation diagrams, state time graphs, lyapunov exponent graph and phase portraits. To handle the chaotic behaviour observed in the non-linear dynamics of the Tuberculosis systems, we use a master–slave method where identical systems are considered. We also design an adaptive controller to achieve global synchronization between the two systems. The results are based on adaptive control theory and lyapunov stability theory. While the framework is mostly theoretical, it provides insights into how chaos-based control mechanisms can be used to analyze complex epidemiological dynamics and may support the future development of adaptive intervention strategies under uncertain conditions in tuberculosis modelling. Numerical simulations are performed in MATLAB which validates the theoretical results and also confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Hyperchaotic Privacy-Preserving Cooperative Adaptive Control With Application to Multimotor Systems

inst.name: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

abstract: This article investigates the privacy-preserving cooperative adaptive control problem for nonlinear multiagent systems with unknown disturbances. First, by leveraging the hyperchaotic phenomenon of the Lorenz–Stenflo system, a masking function is proposed, which endows it with uncertainty and unpredictability and thus greatly improves the encryption performance. Meanwhile, a time-assist function is designed to achieve privacy protection within a preassigned period, which enhances the flexibility of the mechanism. In addition, according to the gradient descent method, a dynamically self-adjustable gain parameter is designed in the disturbance observer. The utilization of this parameter enables the proposed observer not only to handle unknown disturbances, but also to better improve the performance of the system. Afterward, the Lyapunov stability theorem is utilized to prove that all signals of the closed-loop system are semiglobally uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, experimental results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, which successfully accomplishes speed synchronization across multiple permanent magnet synchronous motors, thereby ensuring secure data transmission.

title: Specialized parallel pathways for adaptive control of visual object pursuit
abstract: To pursue a moving visual object, the brain must continuously steer the object to the center of the visual field via feedback. The gain of this control loop is flexible, yet the biological mechanisms underlying such adaptive control are not well understood. Here, we show that adaptive control in the Drosophila pursuit system involves two parallel pathways. One detects objects in the periphery and steers them toward the center of the visual field. The other detects objects near the center of the visual field and steers them to the visual midline while also increasing forward velocity. This latter pathway is flexible: gain increases when the object is moving away from the midline and when the pursuer is running fast-situations that demand rapid steering-and this pathway is preferentially recruited during arousal. Our findings demonstrate how adaptive control can emerge from parallel sensory-motor pathways with specialized properties.

title: A Measure-Valued HJB Perspective on Bayesian Optimal Adaptive Control
venue: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization
topics: Stability and Controllability of Differential Equations
abstract: Abstract. We consider a Bayesian adaptive optimal stochastic control problem where a hidden static signal has a nonseparable influence on the drift of a noisy observation. Being allowed to control the specific form of this dependence, we aim at optimizing a cost functional depending on the posterior distribution of the hidden signal. Our setup is in sharp contrast to existing work: we include costs that depend on the full posterior distribution in a form that admits a large class of nonlinear relationships. Expressing the dynamics of this posterior distribution in the observation filtration, we embed our problem into a genuinely infinite-dimensional stochastic control problem using measure-valued martingales. We address this problem by use of viscosity theory and approximation arguments. Specifically, we show equivalence to a corresponding weak formulation, characterize the optimal value of the problem in terms of the unique continuous viscosity solution of an associated HJB equation, and construct a piecewise constant and arbitrarily-close-to-optimal control to our main problem of study. As a by-product of our analysis, we also provide a novel stability result for a class of measure-valued SDEs which we believe is of independent interest.

title: Neural process model predictive control
abstract: Neural Processes (NPs) can model distributions over functions, like Gaussian Processes, but with the great flexibility and evaluation speed of neural networks. They can be trained purely on data and without prior knowledge. Yet, their architecture allows for a certain degree of interpretability and modular use. We use an NP to model the dynamics in a nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme. After meta-training the NP on data from various system instances, deployment to an unseen system is highly efficient in terms of data and computation. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our NP-MPC scheme for real-time adaptive control, we deploy it to a physical two-axis pendulum experiment requiring short sampling times.

title: A construction-free coordinate-descent augmented-Lagrangian method for embedded linear MPC based on ARX models

inst.name: IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca
IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca

abstract: This paper proposes a construction-free algorithm for solving linear MPC problems based on autoregressive with exogenous terms (ARX) input-output models. The solution algorithm relies on a coordinate-descent augmented Lagrangian (CDAL) method previously proposed by the authors, which we adapt here to exploit the special structure of ARX-based MPC. The CDAL-ARX algorithm enjoys the construction-free feature, in that it avoids explicitly constructing the quadratic programming (QP) problem associated with MPC, which would eliminate construction cost when the ARX model changes/adapts online. For example, the ARX model parameters are dependent on linear parameter-varying (LPV) scheduling signals, or recursively adapted from streaming input-output data with cheap computation cost, which make the ARX model widely used in adaptive control. Moreover, the implementation of the resulting CDAL-ARX algorithm is matrix-free and library-free, and hence amenable for deployment in industrial embedded platforms. We show the efficiency of CDAL-ARX in two numerical examples, also in comparison with MPC implementations based on other general-purpose quadratic programming solvers.

title: BRACE: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control for Safe Navigation under Unknown Disturbances
abstract: Disturbances encountered during autonomous navigation generally vary across space, often discontinuously, as obstacles redirect wind and changing terrain alters traction. Tracking controllers typically assume sufficient control authority to mitigate disturbances and maintain safety; the regime where this assumption fails remains underexplored. We present Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control (BRACE), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances. BRACE infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and uses that to condition a high-level policy that adapts the reference trajectory. The policy combines a nominal and a belief-guided residual term, trained jointly with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic. We evaluate BRACE in three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields, and validate it on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances. Across these settings, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance over model predictive control and RL baselines.

title: Asymmetries in individuals with lower limb amputation are not explained by muscle co-contraction. A pilot study
abstract: Introduction: Maintaining upright posture in humans is challenging because of the high centre of mass and the small base of support. Muscle activation is modulated according to task demands and body orientation relative to gravity. Studying the effect of changes in gravity allows the identification of weight-bearing mechanisms that can inform rehabilitation and technical solutions (e.g., prosthesis) for humans on Earth and in space. In the laboratory, changes in body orientation, such as head-up or head-down tilt, can alter the axial body loading. In this study, we explored balance strategies in individuals with lower-limb amputation under different body loading conditions to (i) understand the nature of the compensatory adjustments often observed in standing and locomotion (Murray et al., 2017) and (ii) the potential adaptations in altered gravity. title: Metabolic heat and moisture reuse with climate-adaptive control for energy-efficient black soldier fly bioconversion in modular container farms

inst.name: Fraunhofer Institute for Molecular Biology and Applied Ecology

abstract: Black soldier fly larvae (BSFL, Hermetia illucens) convert organic residues into feed ingredients and fertiliser. Climate control is a major contributor to the energy demand of container-based bioconversion. We developed a control-oriented dynamic model linking larval growth, substrate dynamics and container climate to heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC). A two-level Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategy planned climate trajectories and tracked them through HVAC actuation. Four simulation studies examined controller selection, HVAC configuration, larval age pairing and inter-container coupling, using subsets of eight climate scenarios. Across the four scenarios tested for controller selection, dynamic MPC reduced specific energy consumption (SEC) by 31 to 61% and increased predicted dry biomass at harvest by up to 27.5% relative to single fixed setpoints. Under the tested controller settings, active cooling was required in the two hot scenarios, whereas dehumidification provided no additional operational benefit. Pairing larval ages four days apart within one container reduced SEC by up to 33% in the tested non-hot scenarios. In the Cooldry scenario, two age-separated containers connected by an actuated air duct produced 9.0% more biomass and achieved 3.9% lower SEC than two independent containers with mixed ages, despite using 4.6% more total HVAC energy. The simulations suggest that dynamic climate control and metabolic heat and moisture reuse can improve the...

title: 200-nm Wavelength-Tracking Operation of a Silicon Photonic Phase Shifter
abstract: The phase shift induced by any kind of integrated photonics phase shifter is inherently wavelength-dependent, limiting the operative spectral bandwidth of any circuit that relies on them. We present a closed-loop adaptive control scheme that automatically compensates for the wavelength-dependent phase dispersion of a thermo-optic phase shifter over a 200 nm spectral range in a silicon photonic Mach–Zehnder interferometer (MZI) switch. The approach is based on a dithering lock-in loop that continuously tracks the optimal operating point as the wavelength is swept across the S, C, and L bands. The control strategy is general and can be applied to a broad class of devices. Using this method, a mean extinction ratio (ER) of the switch above 34 dB over a 1450-1650 nm wavelength span is maintained while tracking laser sweeps up to 200 nm/s. Data transmission experiments with 25 Gbaud NRZ OOK and PAM4 demonstrate that the control maintains signal integrity, whereas an uncontrolled phase shift results in significant eye closure.

title: Barrier-Function-Constrained Residual RL-Based Current Control for LCL-Filtered NPC Inverters under Weak-Grid Operation
abstract: As renewable energy penetration continues to grow, grid-connected inverters are increasingly required to operate reliably under weak-grid conditions, where low short-circuit ratios, changing grid impedances, and rapid disturbances reveal the limitations of conventional fixed-gain PI current controllers. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a more adaptive control approach; however, its application to fast inner current loops remains limited by stringent safety requirements and practical rediness challenges. This paper presents a control framework that combines a model-free Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based residual reinforcement learning controller with a model-based Control Lyapunov Function–Control Barrier Function (CLF–CBF) quadratic-program (QP) safety filter for an LCL-filtered three-phase neutral-point-clamped (NPC) grid-connected inverter. Although residual RL and CLF–CBF safety methods have been explored independently, this work integrates a model-free PPO-based residual controller with a model-based CLF–CBF safety filter within a unified architecture for fast inner-loop current control under varying grid-strength and operating conditions. Instead of replacing the conventional PI controller, the residual policy generates bounded corrective voltage commands that complement a fixed PI baseline, while the CLF–CBF–QP safety filter provides analytical enforcement of stability and operational constraints independently of the learned policy. A two-stage training strateg...

title: Putting the human at the core of human-in-the-loop optimization: integrating clinical expertise and human capacities in exoskeleton learning. An interdisciplinary perspective paper.
abstract: PURPOSE: This interdisciplinary perspective aims to identify key limitations in current Human-in-the-Loop Optimization (HILO) approaches for lower-limb exoskeletons (LLEs) and to propose a shift toward more human-centred optimization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Drawing on literature from wearable robotics, rehabilitation science, motor learning, and clinical practice, we critically discuss three main limitations of current HILO approaches: narrow optimization scope, limited consideration of individual capabilities, and disconnection from personalized training. RESULTS: We argue that human-centered optimization should not only integrate physiotherapists' expertise but also expand their role as research partners in LLE development. Physiotherapists can contribute to adaptive control design, define user-centered outcome measures, and develop evidence-based training protocols that align human learning with technological adaptation. To support this shift, future research should prioritize: (1) using AI to interpret real-time, context-specific and user-specific data; (2) enabling physiotherapists to fine-tune device parameters based on individualized profiles; and (3) embedding structured, therapist-led training within HILO frameworks. CONCLUSION: Advancing human-centered HILO will require adaptable prototypes, multidimensional outcome measures, and sustained collaboration between engineering and rehabilitation science. title: Learning Physical Interaction: A Survey of Tactile- and Force-aware Robot Learning
abstract: Physically grounded robot intelligence requires robots to perceive, reason about, and regulate their interactions with the physical world. This capability is particularly critical in contact-sensitive manipulation, where successful task execution depends not only on visual perception and motion generation, but also on force regulation and adaptive control. In this context, recent robot learning methods have made substantial progress by integrating force, tactile, vision, language, and proprioceptive sensing into learned manipulation policies. In parallel, many systems adopt multi-phase architectures that combine high-level policies, action-refinement modules, and low-level controllers to bridge semantic task understanding with reactive physical execution. Despite these advances, existing surveys have not explicitly reviewed force- and tactile-aware robot learning from a unified perspective that jointly captures multimodal sensing and multi-phase system design. This survey addresses this gap by proposing TF-ART, a Tactile/Force-Aware Robot learning Taxonomy for multimodal and multi-phase frameworks, which maps individual methods into a unified hierarchical structure. The framework characterizes how recent works organize observation modalities, encode and fuse heterogeneous sensory inputs, generate and refine actions across multiple phases, and connect learned policies to reactive robot-end control. Building on this methodological view, we further examine the task settings and ...

title: Ultrasound-assisted wearable patches for transdermal drug delivery
abstract: Abstract Wearable ultrasound patches represent a new class of transdermal drug delivery systems, offering a minimally invasive, programmable, and user-friendly platform for personalized therapy and precision medicine. Here, we review recent advances in ultrasound-assisted transdermal drug delivery (UATDD) with an emphasis on acoustic mechanisms and device engineering. We describe the recent evolution of UATDD from early high-energy sonophoresis to sophisticated, skin-conformal platforms that exploit advanced acoustic modalities for precise, on-demand delivery. Key innovations include bulk-wave, surface acoustic wave, and acoustic vortex-based devices, alongside the synergistic integration of ultrasound with microneedles, which transforms the patch into a localized, in situ therapeutic platform. Looking forward, UATDD systems are poised to evolve toward fully autonomous, closed-loop wearable theranostic platforms that integrate real-time biosensing with artificial intelligence (AI)-driven adaptive control, but challenges remain, including long-term biocompatibility, efficient wireless power management, and clear regulatory pathways. We believe UATDD patches hold significant potential to redefine disease management, shifting the paradigm from intermittent treatment to continuous, adaptive, and autonomous care.

title: Adaptive Linear Quadratic Control of Unknown Linear Time-Varying Systems via Policy Gradient Methods
abstract: Unknown linear time-varying (LTV) systems require the control policy to adapt from online closed-loop data as dynamics evolve. Existing methods usually update the policy by solving a one-shot optimization problem, which can be computationally demanding and sensitive to noisy model estimates. In this paper, we propose a policy gradient adaptive control (PGAC) method for LTV system control with unknown model parameters. Specifically, PGAC integrates online policy optimization into feedback by updating the state-feedback policy with one-step gradient descent of the linear quadratic regulator cost at each time instant. This incremental update is computationally light and naturally limits policy variations caused by noisy data. To explicitly compute the policy gradient online, we estimate local models from recent closed-loop trajectories using normalized sliding-window least-squares. We provide stability and convergence certificates of PGAC for two classes of LTV systems. For slowly time-varying systems, we prove that the closed-loop system achieves practical exponential stability without a dwell-time condition. For piecewise-constant LTV systems, we establish practical stability through a dwell-time contraction argument. We also provide average frozen-time optimality-gap bounds of the policy sequence for both classes. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our method via numerical case studies of both LTV and nonlinear systems.

title: Real-time optimal control with shallow recurrent decoder networks
abstract: Controlling dynamical systems in real-time across multiple scenarios is critical to enabling adaptive control strategies, ensuring stability and efficiency. However, to tailor control actions in response to varying scenarios, traditional optimal control problems typically require several system simulations, which are often computationally demanding due to the high-dimensionality of the underlying spatio-temporal dynamics. In this work, we exploit SHallow REcurrent Decoder networks-based Reduced Order Modeling (SHRED-ROM) to synthesize a real-time closed-loop controller for high-dimensional and parametric dynamics, relying solely on limited state sensor readings. After training the model on a few optimal examples given by an expert demonstrator, SHRED-ROM mimics the expert behavior with effective distributed control actions in new scenarios, alleviating the curse of dimensionality. Moreover, a sensor forecaster is synthesized and used to close the loop at the latent level, thus efficiently mitigating possible sensor failures or delays. The performance of the proposed optimal control strategy is finally assessed on three challenging high-dimensional cases dealing with either parametric density control or fluid flow control.

title: Adaptive Sensorless Strategy for Dual Three-Phase PMSM by the Enhanced Sliding Mode Observer Under Open-Phase Faults
keywords: dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor
abstract: Sensorless control of dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors (DTP-PMSMs) has been extensively investigated to enhance operational reliability. However, when open-phase faults (OPFs) occur, conventional sensorless methods fail to achieve accurate rotor position estimation due to distortions in the back electromotive force (EMF) waveform. These distortions arise from the interruption of voltage signal transmission in the faulted phase, leading to erroneous observer outputs. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes an enhanced sliding mode observer (SMO) incorporating voltage constraints, designed to suppress the back EMF distortion under OPFs. The proposed method ensures robust position estimation by explicitly accounting for the voltage limitations imposed by the faulted phase. Combined with adaptive control strategies, it can also be extended to OPFs of any phase. Experimental results validate that the enhanced SMO maintains high estimation accuracy under OPFs, demonstrating its superiority over conventional methods.

title: Self-driving medicine: closed-loop therapeutics for autonomous disease control
abstract: Closed-loop gene circuits are paving the way toward self-driving medicine: therapeutics that continuously sense physiological signals, compute responses, and autonomously tune therapeutic output. Yet clinical practice still relies largely on open-loop dosing and static interventions that are inherently blind to real-time fluctuations in disease dynamics. Since Paracelsus, medicine has recognized that dose governs both efficacy and toxicity, but closed-loop therapeutics now redefine dose as a continuously computed response to physiology rather than as a fixed schedule. Enabled by synthetic biology, feedback-controlled therapeutics can be built from modular sensors, processors, and effectors to maintain homeostasis around defined physiological setpoints, moving therapy beyond intermittent interventions toward continuous sensing and adaptive control.

title: Neural Network-Augmented Actuation Control System Designed for Path Tracking of Autonomous Underwater-Transportation Systems Under Sensor and Process Noise

inst.name: National University of Sciences and Technology

topics: Control and Dynamics of Mobile Robots
abstract: Underwater-transportation systems have significant potential for both military and commercial applications. Neural Network (NN)-based control offers enhanced robustness for actuators to manage the states of autonomous underwater-transportation systems which include Rigid-Connection Transportation Systems (RCTSs), Flexible-Connection Transportation Systems (FCTSs) and Leader–Follower-Formation Control Transportation Systems (LFFCTSs). In this study, NN-Augmented Control (NNAC) is applied to the aforementioned three transportation systems to enable accurate path tracking by the actuators installed onboard these systems under both ideal operating conditions and in the presence of sensor and process noise. The Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is employed to estimate the system states under noisy conditions. The results demonstrate that NNAC provides robust and adaptive control of actuators, achieving efficient trajectory tracking via the transportation systems despite the influence of sensor and process noise disturbances. NNAC predominance was also observed in comparison with the conventional PID controller. Among the transportation configurations under the NNAC strategy, the RCTS exhibited the highest tracking accuracy with the lowest power consumption by the actuators. The power consumption of actuators installed on the LFFCTS was marginally higher than that of the RCTS. However, the translational motion accuracy of the follower vehicle in the LFFCTS was the lowest due to indirect...

title: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy of Reinforcement Learning-Model Predictive Control Integration for Linear Systems
abstract: The integration of Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for constrained decision-making and adaptive control. MPC offers structured optimization, explicit constraint handling, and established stability tools, whereas RL provides data-driven adaptation and performance improvement in the presence of uncertainty and model mismatch. Despite the rapid growth of research on RL--MPC integration, the literature remains fragmented, particularly for control architectures built on linear or linearized predictive models. This paper presents a comprehensive Systematic Literature Review (SLR) of RL--MPC integrations for linear and linearized systems, covering peer-reviewed and formally indexed studies published until 2025. The reviewed studies are organized through a multi-dimensional taxonomy covering RL functional roles, RL algorithm classes, MPC formulations, cost-function structures, and application domains. In addition, a cross-dimensional synthesis is conducted to identify recurring design patterns and reported associations among these dimensions within the reviewed corpus. The review highlights methodological trends, commonly adopted integration strategies, and recurring practical challenges, including computational burden, sample efficiency, robustness, and closed-loop guarantees. The resulting synthesis provides a structured reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to design or analyze RL--MPC architectures b...

title: A Data-Driven Optimal Control Architecture for Grid-Connected Power Converters
abstract: Grid-connected power converters are ubiquitous in modern power systems, acting as grid interfaces of renewable energy sources, energy storage systems, electric vehicles, high-voltage DC systems, etc. Conventionally, power converters use multiple PID regulators to achieve different control objectives such as grid synchronization and voltage/power regulation, where the PID parameters are usually tuned based on a presumed (and often overly-simplified) power grid model. However, this may lead to inferior performance or even instabilities in practice, as the real power grid is highly complex, variable, and generally unknown. To tackle this problem, we employ a data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) to perform data-driven, optimal, robust, and adaptive control for power converters. We call the converters that are operated in this wayDeePConverters. A DeePConverter can implicitly perceive the characteristics of the power grid from measured data and adjust its control strategy to achieve optimal, robust, and adaptive performance. We present the modular configurations, generalized structure, control behavior specification, inherent robustness, detailed implementation, computational aspects, and online adaptation of DeePConverters. High-fidelity simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests are provided to validate the effectiveness of DeePConverters.

title: Metabolic state and energy reserves jointly regulate adaptive behavioural control

inst.name: Max Planck Institute for Metabolism Research
Max Planck Institute for Metabolism Research
Max Planck Institute for Metabolism Research

abstract: Abstract Animals continuously adapt their behaviour to changing physiological needs through flexible regulation of behavioural control. However, how the energetic state shapes the distinct components of this adaptive control in humans remains poorly understood. Here, we tested how fasting-induced energy deficits and stored energy reserves jointly regulate inhibitory control and incentive motivation in healthy participants. Fasting selectively increased impulsivity for food rewards, an effect attenuated by body fat percentage. In contrast, fasting increased effort expenditure across both food and monetary rewards, revealing a domain-general increase in motivation best explained by relative energy deficit—the ratio of energy expended during fasting to stored energy reserves. Neither effect was explained by changes in subjective reward valuation. Although self-report questionnaires captured stable behavioural tendencies, they failed to account for state-dependent behavioural variation. Together, these findings show that inhibitory control and motivation are governed by distinct metabolic principles operating across different timescales, revealing that adaptive behavioural control depends on the energetic significance of metabolic state rather than on fasting alone.

title: Geometrically Constrained Outlier Synthesis
abstract: Deep neural networks for image classification often exhibit overconfidence on out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. To address this, we introduce Geometrically Constrained Outlier Synthesis (GCOS), a training-time regularization framework aimed at improving OOD robustness during inference. GCOS addresses a limitation of prior synthesis methods by generating virtual outliers in the hidden feature space that respect the learned manifold structure of in-distribution (ID) data. The synthesis proceeds in two stages: (i) a dominant-variance subspace extracted from the training features identifies geometrically informed, off-manifold directions; (ii) a conformally-inspired shell, defined by the empirical quantiles of a nonconformity score from a calibration set, adaptively controls the synthesis magnitude to produce boundary samples. The shell ensures that generated outliers are neither trivially detectable nor indistinguishable from in-distribution data, facilitating smoother learning of robust features. This is combined with a contrastive regularization objective that promotes separability of ID and OOD samples in a chosen score space, such as Mahalanobis or energy-based. Experiments demonstrate that GCOS outperforms state-of-the-art methods using standard energy-based inference on near-OOD benchmarks, defined as tasks where outliers share the same semantic domain as in-distribution data. As an exploratory extension, the framework naturally transitions to conformal OOD inference, whi...

title: ShapeGen3DCP: A deep learning framework for layer shape prediction in 3D concrete printing
topics: Innovations in Concrete and Construction Materials
abstract: This work introduces ShapeGen3DCP , a deep learning framework for fast and accurate prediction of filament cross-sectional geometry in 3D Concrete Printing (3DCP). The method is based on a neural network architecture that takes as input both material properties in the fluid state (density, yield stress, plastic viscosity) and process parameters (nozzle diameter, nozzle height, printing and flow velocities) to directly predict extruded layer shapes. To enhance generalization, some inputs are reformulated into dimensionless parameters that capture underlying physical principles. Predicted geometries are compactly represented using Fourier descriptors, which enforce smooth, closed, and symmetric profiles while reducing the prediction task to a small set of coefficients. The training dataset was synthetically generated using a well-established Particle Finite Element Method (PFEM) model of 3DCP, overcoming the scarcity of experimental data. Validation against diverse numerical and experimental cases shows strong agreement, confirming the machine learning framework’s accuracy and reliability. This opens the way to practical applications, from pre-calibrating print settings and reducing trial-and-error adjustments to optimizing toolpaths for more advanced designs. Looking ahead, coupling the framework with simulations and sensor feedback could enable closed-loop digital twins for 3DCP, driving real-time process optimization, defect detection, and adaptive control of printing parame...

title: From Vision to Assistance: Gaze and Vision-Enabled Adaptive Control for a Back-Support Exoskeleton
